narrative: Reframes patience as the inside view of randomness filtered by selective memory — the ratchet that keeps almost all gains while losing almost none permanently. Moving from Leo Spiegel's CEO boulder-rolling image through evolutionary biology to Whitehead's lure and Teilhard's Omega Point, the chapter argues that the universe's filter is exactly patient: it accepts only what holds, waits as long as needed, and accumulates structures capable of reflection — culminating in the claim that love is what patience builds toward when two reflectors complex enough to notice meet each other.
